Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) and axial CT scans (Figures 2 and 3) demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed mass in the right hemithorax. On the lateral view, the mass forms an obtuse angle with the posterior chest wall, which is a classic radiological sign indicating an extrapulmonary origin (such as from the pleura or chest wall), rather than a pulmonary origin which typically presents with acute angles.
